title: Rank elements by value → ranks over a changing set
label: ag-multi
statement: Replace each element of an array with its **rank**: the smallest value has rank 1, larger values get larger ranks, equal values share a rank, and ranks have no gaps.

stages.title: Rank transform
stages.say: Replace every element with its rank — higher numbers get higher ranks, ties share a rank.

stages.title: Ranks while values change
stages.say: Prices now arrive and leave all day. After each change, what is the rank of a given price? Re-sorting every time is too slow.
stages.require: Add `RankTracker` (values in [0, 1,000,000]): `Add(v)`, `Remove(v)`, `Rank(v)` = distinct values present that are <= v, `Distinct`. Out-of-range → `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
testNames: rank of a value not present
removing an absent value is a no-op

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe sort the distinct values once and map each value to its position for the static version; when values arrive and leave, a Fenwick tree over value presence answers "how many distinct values are at most v" in O(log V). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Rank concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Replace each element of an array with its **rank**: the smallest value has rank 1, larger values get larger ranks, equal values share a rank, and ranks have no gaps.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Do equal values share a rank? (Yes.)
- Dense ranks (no gaps) or competition ranks (1,1,3)? (Dense.)
- Will the set of values change over time? (Stage 2.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A rank is just a position among the distinct values. Once values change over time, "position" becomes "how many distinct values are <= v", which is a prefix count — the job a Fenwick tree does in log time.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "S."ort the distinct values once and map each value to its position for the static version; when values arrive and leave, a Fenwick tree over value presence answers "how many distinct values are at most v" in O(log V)."

learn.title: 5 · Why the approach works

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Competition ranking (1,1,3) when dense was asked.
- Sorting the original array and losing positions.
- Re-sorting after every insert in the dynamic version.
- Counting duplicates twice in a dynamic rank.
